reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Acute isogenic p53 loss and near-endogenous rescue with damage, separate caffeine perturbation, longitudinal cell fate and fixed DNA/incorporation/death assays.

checks.quote: # Proposed Experimental Protocol: Testing Whether p53 Is Necessary and Sufficient for Damage-Induced G1 Arrest in an Isogenic System
checks.reason: No pre-execution consultation of prior detailed Methods/supplements or validated modern protocols with condition-transfer checks. Avoiding historical reconstruction does not remove this requirement.

checks.quote: # Proposed Experimental Protocol: Testing Whether p53 Is Necessary and Sufficient for Damage-Induced G1 Arrest in an Isogenic System
checks.reason: No untagged/TIR1/depletion-reagent matched control separates auxin-system effects from p53 loss, and no caffeine-alone arm supplies the factorial baseline for caffeine interpretation.

checks.quote: caffeine acts through a p53-dependent pathway
checks.reason: Absence of an added caffeine phenotype after p53 depletion can reflect a floor or other pathway interaction; it does not locate caffeine action in a p53 pathway.

checks.quote: genotyping PCR and Sanger sequencing
checks.reason: Engineering/PCR verification lacks amplicon identity/length and reaction/cycling logic, delivery quantities and an operational preparation recipe. Numerical drug/time examples do not supply these chosen core steps.

checks.quote: Prespecified gating strategy
checks.reason: No no-EdU/unstained/single-color/reference calibration and objective accuracy/compensation gate for DNA/incorporation/death measurements; generic named gates do not define assay-calibrated boundaries.

checks.quote: G1 fraction among live cells
checks.reason: The primary endpoint conditions on survivors rather than the original tracked G1 cohort. Excluding death does not remove selective-loss/composition bias, and overlapping sub-G1 plus Annexin-positive events are summed without an explicit union denominator.

checks.quote: n ≈ 4 per group
checks.reason: The stated two-sample 90% power calculation for a 15-point effect, SD 8 and alpha .05 is too small: even the normal approximation requires about six per group, with an exact small-sample t test requiring more. No calibrated alternative justifies four.

checks.quote: Minimum flow events (after gating)
checks.reason: Post-treatment minimum live-event and death cutoffs can exclude precisely the biological response of interest without preserved original-cohort denominators and failure reporting. Retain valid high-death outcomes as uninterpretable for arrest, not selected successful batches.

checks.quote: No significant difference in initial damage load
checks.reason: Nonsignificance is not lesion equivalence. The treated-only primary comparison omits the baseline-by-damage interaction, and cell-level KS/Fisher tests ignore culture clustering. These distinct model/uncertainty defects are charged once under P08.

checks.quote: synonymous mutations in the AID-tag recognition sequence
checks.reason: AID recognition is of the protein degron, so synonymous DNA changes preserve the recognized amino-acid sequence and do not create a degradation-resistant rescue. An untagged or otherwise protein-level resistant rescue is required. Primary mechanism: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19915560/ . The 1-hour damage-marker comparison also need not reflect initial injury before differential repair.

checks.quote: # Proposed Experimental Protocol: Testing Whether p53 Is Necessary and Sufficient for Damage-Induced G1 Arrest in an Isogenic System
checks.reason: Bounded engineering retries are given, but changes are not followed by explicit refreeze and fresh independent confirmation.

checks.quote: If death is phase-uniform, apparent G1 enrichment reflects true arrest
checks.reason: Even phase-uniform death does not make G1 occupancy a residence-time/arrest measurement: altered entry/exit and phase durations can change fractions. The decision must require original-cohort sustained G1 and S-entry outcomes, not merely death-corrected enrichment.

checks.quote: long-term viability independently of short-term arrest
checks.reason: Failure to form colonies can result from persistent viable arrest, so clonogenic loss is not an independent death/viability discriminator. It needs separate sustained viable-state measurement to support that claimed validation role.

checks.quote: # Proposed Experimental Protocol: Testing Whether p53 Is Necessary and Sufficient for Damage-Induced G1 Arrest in an Isogenic System
checks.reason: Plate maps and coded assays omit linked raw tracks/cytometry files, per-cell histories and exact code/gating/model/settings provenance.

checks.quote: # Proposed Experimental Protocol: Testing Whether p53 Is Necessary and Sufficient for Damage-Induced G1 Arrest in an Isogenic System
checks.reason: Clearly proposed study with a concrete AID system, useful dose grids, fixed sampling, randomization/blinding, and practical repair options. However the rescue-resistance mechanism is wrong, the primary survivor fraction cannot distinguish arrest from composition, and power/equivalence/clustering are flawed. Alternative measurements are present but not used in a valid primary decision. Specific tool/endpoint/decision penalties are not duplicated under general G1/G3/G4.
